title: Operational Flows and Policy Gallery
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose and scope:

This page consolidates company-wide operational flows and reusable policy artifacts relating to access and permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended as a single-entry reference for teams to discover the canonical process, required approvals, and the standard templates used by Redwood Inference.

Audience:
- Engineering, Product, Security, Finance, People Ops, and Procurement partners.
- Team leads and managers who approve access, spend, or changes.

Summary (quick reference):
| Area | Owner | Target SLA / Thresholds | Key system | Approval path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & Permissions | Security + IT | Standard request: 48 hours; Elevated: 5 business days; Emergency: <4 hours | IdentityHub (IAM) | Manager -> Security reviewer -> IAM admin |
| Change Management | Eng-Platform | Standard change window: 02:00–05:00 PST; Emergency changes: immediate runbook | OpsChange | Change owner -> CAB -> Release manager |
| Data Management | Security + Data Platform | Retention: 1y/3y/7y by classification; Backup RPO 24h | DataLake / Vault | Data owner -> Security review |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance-Legal | < $5k: manager; $5k–$75k: procurement; > $75k: exec | ProcureFlow, Spendly | Req -> Procurement -> Finance -> Exec (if needed) |
| Vendor Management | Procurement | Onboarding: 7–14 days | Vendor Portal | Security review -> Procurement -> Contracting |
| Travel & Expenses | People Ops + Finance | Per-diem and policy; pre-approval for > $2k | Spendly | Traveler -> Manager -> Finance |

Note: See "Templates" section at the end for direct links to request and approval forms.

1) Access & Permissions (Identity lifecycle)

Overview:
Redwood centralizes identity and access control to IdentityHub. All access must follow least-privilege principles and be tied to an owner and business justification. Temporary elevated access must have an expiration.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: submits request in IdentityHub with justification and business owner.
- Manager: approves role change and validates business need.
- Security reviewer: performs risk review for privileged access (SRE/infra, customer data, KMS/HSM).
- IAM admin: applies the change and documents in the audit log.

Standard process (step-by-step):
1. Requester files an Access Request in IdentityHub with resource, role, justification, and requested duration.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If no response, escalate to manager's skip-level.
3. If the role is privileged, Security reviewer has 2 business days to respond; may place conditions (MFA, limited scope).
4. IAM admin provisions access. Provisioning events must include ticket ID and expiration.

SLOs and monitoring:
- 90% of standard requests fulfilled within 48 hours.
- Emergency access (investigations, P1 incidents): target same-day (4 hours) turnaround via on-call IAM admin and Security Pager.
- Monthly audit: all privileged roles reviewed quarterly.

Exceptions and emergency process:
- Emergency access uses the Emergency Access Runbook (link: OpsChange/Emergency-Access-Runbook). Every emergency grant must be accompanied by an audit ticket and post-incident access review within 7 days.

2) Change Management (Services & Infra)

Purpose:
To minimize risk from configuration and code changes by standardizing assessment, scheduling, and rollouts.

Change categories:
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk, follow templated rollout (e.g., dependency bumps, non-prod config changes).
- Normal changes: require CAB review; typically feature deploys, infra patches.
- Emergency changes: require immediate action; follow Emergency Change runbook and postmortem.

Approval matrix and windows:
- Standard changes: no CAB if they match the Standard Change Catalogue and use a validated automation playbook.
- Normal changes: submit in OpsChange 72 hours before planned window. CAB meets daily for fast lanes and weekly for large changes.
- Change window: default maintenance window 02:00–05:00 PST; services with global usage must consult SRE before scheduling.

Rollback policy:
- All normal and emergency changes must include a rollback plan and a success metric (SLO delta or error rate).
- If errors exceed alert threshold (error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline), trigger rollback and incident response.

Post-change verification:
- Owner must run the Post-Change Checklist in OpsChange within 4 hours of completion and mark the change as successful or failed.

3) Data Management (Classification, Retention, Access)

Classification table:
| Classification | Examples | Default retention | Access controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Marketing assets | 0 | Read-only public URLs |
| Internal | Documentation, non-sensitive logs | 3 years | Corporate SSO with RBAC |
| Confidential | Customer PII, analytics with identifiers | 7 years | Justified access, strict logging, DLP |
| Restricted | KMS keys, secrets, regulated customer data | As required by contract | Restricted to named individuals, HSM/KMS controls |

Data handling requirements:
- PII and Confidential datasets require a documented Data Processing Agreement and must be stored only in Vault-backed buckets with encryption at rest.
- Backups: daily snapshot with retention according to classification. Restore drills: annually for Restricted data, bi-annually for Confidential.

Retention and deletion:
- Automated retention policies are enforced via DataLife jobs. Data owners must declare retention period at onboarding.
- Deletion requests use the Data Deletion Template and are tracked in the Data Deletion Register.

Data change control:
- Schema migrations that touch production must be submitted to Data Platform and follow the Migration Review workflow (submit migration PR, canary run, monitoring).

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <$5,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow (Spendly card optional).
- $5,000–$75,000: Procurement team approval + Finance-Legal review (Supplier terms assessment).
- >$75,000: Procurement + Finance-Legal + Executive approval (SVP or CFO).
- Capital spend: follow Capitalization policy; enter requisition with finance tag.

Competitive sourcing and vendor evaluation:
- For purchases > $50k, obtain at least 2 competitive quotes and document selection rationale in ProcureFlow.
- Risk scoring: Procurement assigns a Vendor Risk Score (1–10). Any vendor with score >=7 triggers Security review and may require SOC2/ISO evidence.

Expense reimbursement rules (high level):
- Use Spendly to submit expense reports. Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Per-diem for domestic travel: $75/day lodging cap: $250/night without pre-approval.
- International travel: pre-approval required for trips exceeding $2,000.

Audit and controls:
- Monthly reconciliation between ProcureFlow and accounting.
- Random sample expense audits quarterly (finance + internal audit).

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding checklist (7–14 day target):
1. Vendor request created in Vendor Portal (ProcureFlow) with SOW/quote.
2. Procurement performs commercial review and risk scoring.
3. Security runs technical and compliance review (SOC2/penetration test evidence as required).
4. Legal reviews contract terms and data processing clauses.
5. Finance provisions payment terms and payment method.
6. Account team verifies go/no-go.

Contractual controls and SLAs:
- Standard contract must include: data residency clause, breach notification timeline (<=72 hours), liability caps, and SLA definitions (uptime, support response).
- For production services that affect customer traffic, require 99.9% uptime SLA and a runbook integration.

Offboarding and termination:
- On contract end, Procurement triggers Offboarding Checklist: license termination, access revocation in IdentityHub, data return or secure deletion, final invoice settlement.

6) Travel policy (concise)

Pre-approval:
- Any trip expected to exceed $2,000 requires manager & finance pre-approval via Spendly.

Travel safety and insurance:
- All employees traveling on business automatically receive Redwood travel insurance and are covered under the company incident response procedures.

Booking and allowable expenses:
- Use company preferred vendors where available. Personal upgrades should not be charged to company cards without explicit manager approval.

Expense timelines:
- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip completion. Late submissions may delay reimbursement.

7) Templates and artifacts (canonical)

Available templates (ProcureFlow / Confluence Templates):
- Access Request Template (IdentityHub Request Form) -> /confluence/templates/access-request-template
- Change Request Template (OpsChange Change Form) -> /confluence/templates/change-request-template
- Data Deletion Request -> /confluence/templates/data-deletion-request
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist -> /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Low-value Purchase Requisition (<$5k) -> /confluence/templates/requisition-lowvalue
- Expense Report Template (Spendly) -> /confluence/templates/expense-report-template

Example JSON/YAML snippets:
- Minimal change request example (YAML):
---
title: "Upgrade dependency X"
components: [service-a, service-b]
window: "2026-09-01T02:00:00-07:00 to 2026-09-01T05:00:00-07:00"
rollback: "helm rollback v1"
owner: "team-service-owner@example.com"
---

Audit and enforcement:
- Policy exceptions must be recorded using the Exception Request Template and approved by the policy owner. Exceptions are logged and reviewed quarterly.
- Non-compliance (unapproved access, unauthorized spend) escalates to the owner_team and may be subject to disciplinary action per HR policy.

Operational readiness and playbooks:
- Each area above has an associated runbook stored in OpsChange and linked from this page. Runbooks include command snippets, contact on-call rotation, and verification checks.
